decisions.decision: Drop contrastive /ə/. Allow [ə] only as a non-contrastive reduction or accent realization where identity is preserved.
Use lexical /a e i o u/. Prefer /a i u/ for grammar-critical contrasts where practical.

Retain canonical /j/ as a lexical glide. Carry /w/ forward as the strong default lexical glide candidate; its final freeze remains pending the remaining inventory-wide checks. Orthographic graphemes remain a separate decision.
Use one rhotic category /r/ with broad acceptable rhotic realizations; do not prescribe trill, tap, approximant, or uvular realization.
Retain /b d ɡ v z ʃ/ as lexical candidates subject to protected-minimal-pair rules; do not rely on their fragile merger contrasts for critical grammar.

Do not assign independent phoneme status to /ts tʃ dʒ/. Represent [ts] from /t+s/; allow /t+j/ to surface as [tj ~ tʃ] and /d+j/ as [dj ~ dʒ]. The transparent sequence pronunciation remains valid, and none of these coalescences may carry grammar-critical contrasts.

Use i/u/a for first/second/third person. Mark plural with a nasal morphophoneme /N/ written n after the person vowel: i, u, a; in, un, an. In neutral forms /N/ is normally word-final; it may be medial specifically before the optional referential-specificity suffixes -o/-e, yielding forms such as ano/ane. Default [n]; accent-tolerant place realizations [n ~ ɳ ~ m ~ ŋ ~ ɴ] are non-contrastive and may not be deleted.

Keep grammatical gender neutral by default with zero marking. Optionally mark masculine/male-specific reference with -o and feminine/female-specific reference with -e; these are semantic/referential specificity markers, not grammatical gender classes, and never trigger obligatory agreement. The neutral form always remains valid. Third person is a/ao/ae in the singular and an/ano/ane in the plural, with morphological order person + plural N + optional specificity marker. Accent-tolerant realizations may raise canonical -e toward [i] and -o toward [u] where mid vowels are unstable, but the front/back distinction must remain recoverable and the two markers may not collapse when the distinction is intended; otherwise use the neutral form or lexical paraphrase.
